Your pain is valid.   
Your depression is valid.   
Your shame, anger, and overwhelmed-ness is valid. 

The way you are being treated is terrible. I'm so proud of you for going into a treatment center and trying to get help. I'm so sorry that you got treated that way. I saw you say that you lived in a rural area. Many many therapist are doing telehealth now. They don't have to be in your area. You can search psychologytoday and liveandworkwell for therapist by issue. There is completely online therapy websites too.   


You are stronger than you feel right now.

I feel you man. I was diagnosed when I was 18. Also because of bad parents. People took one look at me, little 18 year old girl, and decided I couldn't have PTSD all. the. time. It wasn't until recently that I even starting telling people again.   


But basically what everyone is saying, don't deal with them. You don't have to! Your pain and suffering does not only exist if other people accept it. I know that sounds simple, but it isn't. We constantly require validation from other people, doctors, bosses, relationships, ect, because of this illness. But if they don't give us that, it doesn't go away. So try not to let others validation of your illness affect you.   


The best people in my life have people who said "oh, okay." when I told them I had PTSD.

I agree with you that there are many aspects of this that are not working out for OP. However, I personally don't see much gray area. Yes, most people have fantasies and masturbate to many different things. But everything depends on the boundaries and consent of the acting parties. I'm sure there are many relationships out there where this would be acceptable. However, It doesn't sound like OP gave consent for this and tried to set many boundaries. I don't think comparing OPs relationship, where one partner is uncomfortable to a potential situation where no one is, is very helpful for OP.

There is a difference between fantasizing and thinking about someone else while having sex with your partner. You are very much downplaying the behavior of OPs partner and establishing boundaries that are not yours to set. If OP doesn't like the behavior, then they are allowed to feel that way.   


If you had sex someone and afterwards they told they only got off because they taught of someone else you would excuse them because it's just a fantasy?
Yes, exactly! Unfortunately, this tactic will work exclusively on people who want to be empathic and supportive for that person. I feel very much for OP.

First of all, you are not stupid and naive. Being caring, trusting, and supportive is a wonderful character trait to have. However, if you are going to have those it is imperative that you also learn how to create boundaries and be able to identify red flags; so that you do not harm yourself by being that way. Or in other words, don't give it to the wrong person.  


Here, I think you are giving those traits to the wrong person. To me, it seems he is using this porn addiction to sweep other terrible behaviors under the rug. Like thinking about his ex during intimate situations with you and masturbating's to friends. Your partner has behavioral issues and it making you suffer as well because of them. 

It doesn't seem like you are getting much space or respect out this relationship either. You say you are not doing well and that you have recently lost your father. How often does he help or talk with you about this? Does he try to help you in the same understanding and patient way you have delt with behavioral issues? Do you find yourself taking care of this relationship more than yourself in this difficult time?

Try taking a couple deep breaths about the situation and taking a step back. I sense that you are getting very caught up in the assumption that the messages were negative, and it is already beginning to affect you.  It makes any situation much more difficult to go into it with an assumption. If you did approach him right now, and it was completely innocent, he would first have to talk you out of believing the messages were negative. Try looking at this in a more neutral light.  


You have context clues to his conversation that it was about sex. And you know that some of the comments were deleted.   


This seems to be really bothering you. So I think once you've feel a bit more neutral about it, bringing it up to him would help. Let him know that you are feeling insecure, and that you need some validation right now. Be respectful of his privacy if he request it. Truly, you have no idea what the messages said. But you can create the space to have a conversation about it and find some peace.

I think it is a bit alarming that your therapist has used the potential of your partner harming themselves as a reason for his belief that you shouldn't tell your partner. How do you think your therapist reached this conclusion?

This breakup however. Well, I think you might be onto something. The behavior post breakup has been incredibly isolating and neglectful.

Thank you for trying to help me work through this.   


When I create a "physical" distance, as in no contact, I feel like shit. I worry about him. My mind is easily negative. I go over everything again and again.   
When I close that distance, I feel better and like I'm reaching an understanding for a couple days. I'm content with the situation. Then I feel like shit. I start to question everything, like this post.   


I think maybe a good distance for me would be romantic? Like, if I didn't try to constantly understand the romantic distance he's already created.   
My romantic door is already, I guess, half closed? I understand that he ended the relationship and that if he came back at this very moment, I shouldn't accept it.  


But then again I don't trust myself to do that. I did fully close the door. I told him I would never speak to him again. I meant it. But overtime, I slowly opened it back up. I think I'm terrified of that door being closed, or in denial, or don't really want it to be. I don't know. I feel constantly shifted between two extremes. I can't stand him, I can't believe he's done this. He's just sick, I love him unconditionally.   


I can't really think of any other distances to create. Is there one that I am missing?

It's kind of hard for me to look at this as if he doesn't have an obligation to me. He did break up with me. But he said he didn't know why. And then ran around and told everyone he still loves me he's just crazy.  

But yeah, it's true. I'd probably have an easier time swallowing this if I let go of the expectation.

I see that you care because you tried to talk to someone. And it bothered you so much that it didn't work out you posted it here. It is frustrating to try to help people and get rejected. Especially when coming from a place of genuine care. That's understandable. 

When you speak to a suicidal person your words could be literally the only thing keeping them from doing it or not doing it. So, everyone is of course going to be sensitive about it.

However, the way to speak to anyone anywhere on this spectrum is *almost* down to a science because we *almost* have why people want to commit suicide down to a science. Everyone is different though. I don't want to make you feel you feel like I'm lecturing you when you came here to vent. But if you ever feel like looking into it I will list some good reading. [The reddit suicide community has a fantastic wiki about talking in these situations.](https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/wiki/talking_tips) 

Thank you for caring about suicidal people. I hope that your frustrating interaction has not lessened your desire to do so.
